courses.title: Marketing Principles
courses.description: A foundational marketing course built around the 4Ps, customer behavior, ethics, sustainability, and global cultural context.

courses.title: Molecular Biology
courses.description: Cell signaling, transcription, translation, gene regulation, and molecular techniques with an emphasis on experiment interpretation.

courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: Processes, concurrency, synchronization, memory management, virtualization, and file systems through systems-level problem solving.

nodes.evidenceSummary: Strong grasp of the marketing definition and value exchange framing.
Comfortable with the structure, but still mixing strategic and tactical examples.
Can identify strengths and weaknesses but needs cleaner external-versus-internal framing.
Still needs repetition on customer versus consumer and decision influences.
Recognizes core cases but needs stronger justification when applying them to scenarios.
Developing sense of how cultural variation changes promotion and positioning choices.
Comfortable moving between DNA, RNA, and protein-level reasoning.
Understands polymerase directionality and proofreading, but helicase/primase coordination is still shaky.
Can name the regulatory pieces, but enhancer and promoter roles still blur together.
Good ribosome-process recall, but codon-to-anticodon checking still needs confidence.
Needs more practice connecting primer specificity to expected band patterns.
Still building comfort interpreting expression data across multiple molecular techniques.
Solid understanding of process state, PCB fields, and why context switches cost time.
Can compare policies, but still needs more speed on turnaround versus response tradeoffs.
Race-condition reasoning is improving, but semaphore ordering questions still trip you up.
Address translation is decent, but TLB and replacement policy tradeoffs still need review.
You can describe inodes and journaling, but need sharper crash-recovery reasoning.
This is the biggest gap right now, especially tracing interleavings and deadlock prevention.

sessions.title: Marketing Principles Introduction
sessions.summary: Reviewed the AMA definition of marketing and connected it to the course framing: creating, communicating, delivering, and exchanging value for customers and society at large.

sessions.title: 4Ps and Course Goals Review
sessions.summary: Studied the course overview from the first lecture deck, focusing on Product, Place, Price, and Promotion as the backbone of strategy analysis and exam prep.

sessions.title: Customer vs Consumer Deep Dive
sessions.summary: Worked through the opening classroom prompt on who counts as a customer versus a consumer, tying it back to needs, wants, and marketing myopia.

sessions.title: Ethics, Culture, and Sustainability
sessions.summary: Connected the syllabus case material to likely exam themes: Cambridge Analytica for data ethics, Starbucks for cultural nuance, The True Cost for sustainability, and Eat Ugly for social-impact promotion.

sessions.title: Exam 1 Foundations Review
sessions.summary: Consolidated early-semester material into a study checkpoint covering the 4Ps, SWOT, portfolio thinking, buyer behavior, loyalty, and customer-driven strategy.

sessions.title: DNA Replication and Polymerases
sessions.summary: Reviewed leading versus lagging strand synthesis, polymerase directionality, Okazaki fragments, and how proofreading supports replication fidelity.

sessions.title: Transcription and Gene Regulation
sessions.summary: Focused on promoters, transcription factors, RNA polymerase, and the differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic regulation.

sessions.title: Translation and the Ribosome
sessions.summary: Worked through codons, tRNA charging, initiation, elongation, and where translation errors can disrupt protein structure.

sessions.title: PCR and Gel Electrophoresis Review
sessions.summary: Connected denaturation, annealing, extension, primer specificity, and band interpretation to the upcoming molecular techniques practical.

sessions.title: Processes, Threads, and Context Switching
sessions.summary: Compared processes and threads, reviewed PCB fields, and stepped through how the scheduler and context switch overhead affect performance.

sessions.title: Locks, Semaphores, and Deadlock
sessions.summary: Worked through race conditions, mutexes, semaphore signaling, and the Coffman deadlock conditions with operating-system examples.

sessions.title: Virtual Memory and Paging
sessions.summary: Covered address translation, page tables, TLB behavior, page faults, and the tradeoffs behind replacement strategies.

sessions.title: File Systems and I/O Review
sessions.summary: Reviewed inodes, directory structures, caching, journaling, and the relationship between disk layout and crash recovery.
